title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: choose which AI apps the generative AI apps indicators monitor
summary: The administrator paths, command, defaults and billing statements are supported by Microsoft documentation, and the release details match the roadmap. Remove the unsupported comparison with earlier monitoring behaviour and cite the settings overview for the statement that settings apply across all policies.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Administrators can select individual apps to include or exclude from generative AI indicator monitoring.
claims.quote: For Microsoft Copilot experiences and Enterprise AI apps, you can select which specific generative AI apps you want to monitor.

claims.claim: Before this change, the indicators monitored every available app rather than allowing app selection.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "previously" "apps" "monitor"; opened the policy indicators, getting-started and policy templates pages. They describe current selection and defaults, not the earlier monitoring behaviour.
claims.fix: Remove ', instead of monitoring every available app' from the first sentence of What's changing; retain the documented statement that administrators can choose individual apps.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot experiences includes Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio and connected or cloud AI applications.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot experiences: Support for user interactions in Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio, any connected or cloud AI application.

claims.claim: Enterprise AI apps are non-Copilot AI applications connected using Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Purview Data Map connectors.
claims.quote: Enterprise AI apps: Non-Copilot AI applications connected using Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Purview Data Map connectors.

claims.claim: Other AI applications are discovered from users' browser activity.
claims.quote: Other AI applications: AI applications that users in your organization discover from their browser activity.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Per-app selection applies only to Microsoft Copilot experiences and Enterprise AI apps, not Other AI applications.
claims.quote: For Microsoft Copilot experiences and Enterprise AI apps only, you can review and deselect apps to optimize costs and reduce alert noise.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: All available apps are selected by default.
claims.quote: By default, all available apps are selected.

claims.claim: The app-selection control is admin-opt-in: it excludes no available app until an administrator configures exclusions.
claims.quote: By default, all available apps are selected. You can deselect apps that aren't relevant to your organization to reduce alert noise and avoid unnecessary pay-as-you-go billing charges.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Deselected apps' signals, including prompts and responses, are no longer processed by these indicators.
claims.quote: Use these indicators in policies to analyze interactions (prompts and responses) entered into these applications ... When an app is deselected, signals from that app aren't processed and no cost is incurred.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing: Spend control; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Deselecting an app prevents charges for processing that app's signals with these indicators.
claims.quote: When an app is deselected, signals from that app aren't processed and no cost is incurred.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Insider Risk Management settings are tenant-wide and apply across policies regardless of template.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management settings apply to all Insider Risk Management policies, regardless of the template you choose when creating a policy.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-settings to sources as 'Learn about Insider Risk Management settings'; it directly supports the cross-policy scope statement.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[1].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The Enterprise AI apps indicator requires enabling pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: To use the Enterprise AI apps indicator, enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[1].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot experiences indicator requires pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data.
claims.quote: To use the Microsoft Copilot experiences indicator for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions
claims.claim: Detecting risky interactions in Microsoft 365 Copilot data has no pay-as-you-go requirements or charges.
claims.quote: There aren't any pay-as-you-go billing requirements or charges for Microsoft 365 detecting inappropriate or risky interaction for Microsoft 365 Copilot data.

claims.claim: Administrators must verify that the organization has a supported subscription for Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: To access and use Insider Risk Management, administrators need to verify their organization has a supported subscription and assign the appropriate licenses to users.

claims.claim: The getting-started page requires assigning appropriate licenses to users and links to subscription requirements.
claims.quote: assign the appropriate licenses to users. For more information about subscriptions and licensing, see the subscription requirements for Insider Risk Management.

claims.claim: The getting-started page offers a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 trial to organizations without that plan.
claims.quote: If you don't have an existing Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 plan and want to try Insider Risk Management, you can add Microsoft 365 to your existing subscription or sign up for a trial of Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Mixed licensing reflects Insider Risk Management's use of per-user licensing, pay-as-you-go billing or both.
claims.quote: This feature uses pay-as-you-go billing or per-user licensing for Microsoft Purview capabilities or both.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Insider Risk Management cloud and generative AI policy indicator processing uses Data Security processing units measured daily.
claims.quote: | Insider Risk Management | Detect risky behavior for non-Microsoft 365 locations when using Cloud and generative AI policy indicators | Data Security processing unit as measured on a daily basis |

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing requires associating the Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go charges appear in an Azure bill generated monthly.
claims.quote: An Azure bill is generated at the end of the month for the total number of pay-as-you-go charges across all Microsoft solutions.

claims.claim: The billing models page directs readers to Microsoft's Purview pricing page for pricing.
claims.quote: Understand pricing and estimate your expected monthly costs for pay-as-you-go capabilities: Microsoft pay-as-you-go pricing

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Who configures it
claims.claim: Global Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Organization Management have the same solution permissions as Insider Risk Management Admins.
claims.quote: Members of the following roles can assign users to Insider Risk Management role groups and have the same solution permissions included with the Insider Risk Management Admins role group:

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: App selection is at Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators > Generative AI apps indicators > Choose apps to monitor.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators. ... Expand Generative AI apps indicators. ... For Microsoft Copilot experiences and Enterprise AI apps, select Choose apps to monitor.

claims.claim: No Security & Compliance PowerShell cmdlet or Microsoft Graph operation is documented for setting this app selection.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "insider" "indicators" "settings"; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "InsiderRisk" "indicator". Opened policy indicators and settings pages; no app-selection setter found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Global generative AI indicators are configured at Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators > Generative AI apps indicators.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators. ... Expand Generative AI apps indicators.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation to enable these global indicator settings.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell insider risk management policy indicators generative AI enable settings; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "insider" "indicators" "settings". Opened policy indicators and settings pages; no enabling operation found.

claims.claim: All global indicators are disabled by default.
claims.quote: All global indicators are disabled by default; you must select one or more indicators to configure an Insider Risk Management policy.

claims.claim: Role-group membership is configured at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane. ... Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds membership in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The usage report is at Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Reports > Pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: The following reports are available by navigating to Insider Risk Management > Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal: ... Pay-as-you-go: Review pay-as-you-go usage reports to identify cost-saving opportunities and fine-tune your policy configurations.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent is documented for the Insider Risk Management billed-processing report.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management pay-as-you-go usage report Microsoft Graph API PowerShell export. Opened reports, billing models and Usage center pages; results document portal reporting and unrelated alert-export APIs, not an API for this report.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; Cost and licensing: Spend control; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Pay-as-you-go report breaks billed processing down by data source category and activity indicator over time.
claims.quote: The reports let you explore granular breakdowns of billed processing usage across different data source categories and activity indicators over time.
